newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London steady, await economic data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London steady, await economic data.

text.p: U.S. shares in London were little changed on Thursday from New York closing levels with many European players sidelined ahead of consumer price and industrial production figures due later, dealers said.
"There hasn't been a lot going on this morning. People aren't going to do much until they see the CPI data," one dealer said.
U.S. consumer prices, excluding food and energy, are expected to rise by 0.2 percent in April with the year-on-year CPI seen at 2.6 percent, according to a Reuters poll of economists.
The CPI data, due at 1230 GMT, is followed by industrial production and capacity utilisation figures, out at 1415 GMT.
Industrial production is forecast to rise by 0.2 percent in April while capacity utilisation is seen at 84.1 percent -- both estimates unchanged from the previous month.

"If the data meets expectations we should see the Dow start higher," the dealer said. "But Wall Street still looks a bit overbought in the short-term so I wouldn't be too surprised if the market ended lower tonight."
Only a handful of shares had traded by 1030 GMT.
IBM was up $1/4 to $174-1/2 while Intel Corp added $1/4 to $153.
Philip Morris Cos Inc was $1/8 higher at $42-4/8.
